We need to create parameterized tests for many cases. Use Mockito to mock Indicator<Num> delegate for cases like null return, different Num implementation, NaN, Infinity, custom exception, etc.

We also need to test behavior when delegate is null (NumericIndicator.of(null) should cause NPE on getValue). Since NumericIndicator.of returns a NumericIndicator wrapping delegate; we can create via new NumericIndicator(null) maybe there is a constructor? Not shown but there is likely a static of method that returns new NumericIndicator(delegate). We'll assume we can use NumericIndicator.of(null) and then call getValue.

We also need to test mutable delegate state: after initial call, modify underlying series; but we can mock delegate to return a value then later change stub.

Also test reference equality.

Edge cases: index negative, out of range; we need to set up mock to throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

We need to keep existing @BeforeAll that sets up series and numericIndicator for simple delegation test; but for other tests we may need separate NumericIndicator instances with mocked delegate. Use @Nested test classes or separate test methods.

We'll create parameterized test method using @MethodSource to supply arguments per group.

Define a static class TestCase with fields: int index; Object expected; String description; Class<? extends Throwable> expectedException; Num expectedNum; etc. But easier: create separate test methods for each group.

Simplify: Write parameterized test for normal delegation (valid indices) using real series; already have test.

Write test for exception propagation using mock delegate that throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for -1, 10, Integer.MAX_VALUE.

Write test for null return using mock delegate returning null.

Write test for different Num implementation: we can create a custom Num implementation e.g., using DecimalNum.valueOf but we need DoubleNum; library may have DoubleNum class. Not sure; we can use DecimalNum.valueOf(7.89) which is DecimalNum still. For demonstration we can create a mock Num object.

Better: Use Mockito to mock Num and stub toString or value; but we can check instance type.

Write test for NaN and Infinity: DecimalNum.NaN and DecimalNum.POSITIVE_INFINITY.

Write test for custom unchecked exception: create class CustomRuntimeException extends RuntimeException.

Write test for reference equality: mock delegate returns a specific Num object; assert same reference.

Write test for mutable delegate: Use a mock delegate that returns value first, then we change stub after call; verify original value returned.

Write test for null delegate: NumericIndicator.of(null) and expect NPE.

We'll keep existing @BeforeAll for series.

We'll add @Nested classes for organization.

Implementation details:

- For mock delegate: Indicator<Num> mockDelegate = Mockito.mock(Indicator.class);

- Stub getValue(index) using Mockito.when(mockDelegate.getValue(index)).thenReturn(num) or thenThrow.

- For mutable delegate: Use an AtomicReference<Num> ref = new AtomicReference<>(DecimalNum.valueOf(55)); Mockito.when(mockDelegate.getValue(3)).thenAnswer(invocation -> ref.get()); Then after calling numericIndicator.getValue(3) store result, then ref.set(DecimalNum.valueOf(99)), call again maybe not needed. Verify first result equals 55.

- For null delegate: NumericIndicator numeric = NumericIndicator.of(null); then assertThrows(NullPointerException.class, () -> numeric.getValue(0));

- For index out of range: the mock delegate will throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

- For null return: Mockito.when(mockDelegate.getValue(3)).thenReturn(null); then numericIndicator.getValue(3) returns null.

- For different Num implementation: we can create a custom Num class implementing Num; but easier: use Mockito.mock(Num.class) and stub toString; but we need to verify instance type. We'll just assert same object returned.

- For NaN: DecimalNum.NaN is static? In library maybe DecimalNum.NaN; we can use DecimalNum.NaN. Similarly POSITIVE_INFINITY.
